No web search, no standout source code, no standout repository, and no prior
knowledge of standout internals — I had none to draw on. What I did use beyond
docs/:

- General Rust, clap 4 derive, serde and serde_json knowledge. I added
  `serde_json = { version = "1", features = ["preserve_order"] }` to Cargo.toml
  (the `preserve_order` feature is what makes `-o json` emit the field order
  SPEC.md shows instead of alphabetical).
- rustc/cargo error messages, which is how I confirmed API shapes the docs name
  but do not fully spell out.
- Empirical probing of the framework: before writing the app I built a
  throwaway `spike/` crate in this workspace against the same pinned standout
  9.0.0, ran it, and inspected the resulting stdout/stderr/exit codes with xxd
  to learn how `Output::Render` + template, `Output::Artifact`, and
  `ExternalFailure` actually behave at the process edge. That is black-box
  observation of the binary's behavior, not reading standout's source. The
  spike directory has been deleted.
- General knowledge of kubectl's semantics, used only to pick defaults where
  SPEC.md is silent (listed as assumptions in answer 1). Nothing in the spec's
  stated behavior rests on it.

answers.docs.gaps:
Nothing I found was *wrong*. Three things were missing:

(a) The style-tag/data interaction in answer 4(a). docs/crates/render/topics/
templating.md states the pipeline as "Template + Data → [Pass 1: MiniJinja] →
Text with style tags → [Pass 2: BBParser] → Final output" and documents the
trailing-newline contract to the byte, but says nothing about interpolated data
containing `[...]`. In practice `[b]bb[/b]` in data was consumed as a tag and a
framework warning was written to stderr, in both `--output=auto` and
`--output=term`.

(b) `Output::Artifact`'s interaction with `--output`. docs/crates/dispatch/
topics/handler-contract.md says "Structured modes serialize the same envelope",
which describes the *report*, and leaves open whether the artifact bytes are
also reshaped. Observed: the bytes reach stdout verbatim under `--output json`
and `--output term` alike, which is what the whole design here rests on. Worth
stating, since it is the only seam that gives an application byte-exact stdout.

(c) `allow_stdout()` appears only as prose in the destination-policy list
("stdout, if the application opted in with `allow_stdout()`"), never in a code
sample; the one `Output::Artifact` example uses `suggest_destination(...)`. The
stdout-plus-report shape — which is exactly the "bytes to stdout, report to
stderr" row of docs/topics/execution-outcomes.md — has no worked example.
answers.friction:
(a) The BBCode pass mangles data that happens to contain brackets, and
complains on stderr. With `Output::Render` and a `{{ text }}` template, a view
string containing `[x]` and `[b]bb[/b]` came back as:

    stdout: o=Some("name") json={"items":[{"a":1}]} [x] bb
    stderr:
     Standout :: Warnings
    	Unresolved style tag(s) degraded to unstyled text: b, x

That is fatal for a spec whose contract is "pure JSON on stdout ... never
prefaced with prose" and whose stderr is asserted. docs/crates/render/topics/
templating.md documents the two-pass pipeline and the trailing-newline contract
carefully, but never says what pass 2 does to *data* that looks like a tag, so
I only found this by probing. It is why every command in the finished app
returns `Output::Artifact` instead of `Output::Render`.

(b) Ordinary handler errors cannot carry the spec's stderr line. docs/topics/
error-handling.md: "Standout formats the message as `Error: {error}` — the
error's own `Display` text after that fixed prefix ... and exits with status
`1`." SPEC.md wants exactly `kubelike: pods "nope" not found in namespace
"default"` and, for the cluster-scoped case, exit 2. `Error: ` in front of it
and no way to select status 2 left `ExternalFailure` as the only documented
route to both.

(c) There is no documented way for a *successful* handler to write to stderr.
docs/topics/error-handling.md says "Do not print or call `process::exit` from
handlers", and the framework warning collector described in docs/topics/
execution-outcomes.md is framework-owned with no application-facing emit API
that I could find by grepping. SPEC.md's empty result needs exit 0, empty
stdout, and one prose line on stderr.

(d) `#[handler]` parameter ids versus clap derive field ids. docs/topics/
dispatch-attributes.md warns about this ("Underscores become hyphens ... the
two disagree unless one of them says so"), and it did bite: `all_namespaces`
needed `#[arg(id = "all-namespaces", ...)]` on the clap side to meet the
handler's `all-namespaces`. Documented, but easy to miss.

answers.summary:
`kubelike` is implemented and complete in `app/`. `cargo build` succeeds with no
warnings from the crate, `cargo test` passes 22 unit tests, and I verified every
example in SPEC.md by running the built binary and byte-comparing (xxd) the
tables, the describe blocks, the JSON, and the trailing newlines.

Layout: `src/cluster.rs` (frozen state + kind registry), `src/config.rs`
(kubeconfig reading, the flag > env > kubeconfig > `default` chain),
`src/render.rs` (the one table layout rule and the describe key padding),
`src/core.rs` (all behavior, CLI-free and environment-free — it takes an
already-resolved namespace plus a "did `-n` put it there" bool),
`src/handlers.rs` (`#[handler]` adapters), `src/tests.rs`, `src/main.rs` (clap
`Cli`, a `#[derive(Subcommand, Dispatch)]` tree with `#[dispatch(nested)]` for
`config current-context`, and `App::builder()`).

The command surface, the format vocabulary (`-o` default/`wide`/`name`/`json`/
`custom-columns=`), `-l`, `-A`, the comma-separated kind list judged as one
invocation, the empty-set rules, `api-resources`, `config current-context`, and
the 0/1/2 exit codes all behave as specified. `-o` and `--output` coexist;
`get pods -o name --output text|term` emits identical bytes.

One structural decision drove the rest: every command hands standout its exact
stdout bytes as `Output::Artifact(Artifact::new(bytes).allow_stdout())` rather
than `Output::Render` + template. See the friction and workaround answers.

Assumptions I had to make where SPEC.md is silent, all flagged rather than
hidden: (a) a not-found name on a cluster-scoped kind drops the namespace clause
(`kubelike: nodes "nope" not found`), since a node is in no namespace;
(b) `-o json` is compact single-line, matching how the spec's samples are
written; (c) an unrecognized `-o` value is a domain error (exit 1,
`kubelike: unknown output format "yaml"`) because exit 2 is enumerated for an
unknown *flag*, not an unknown flag *value*; (d) in a mixed kind list, blocks
that match nothing are dropped and the empty-set rule applies only when every
block is empty; (e) an empty `KUBECONFIG`/`KUBELIKE_NAMESPACE` reads as unset.
answers.workarounds:
(a) `ExternalFailure` for ordinary domain errors. docs/topics/error-handling.md
says "Use `ExternalFailure` only when another operation owns the status and
diagnostic contract, such as a delegated Git invocation." No external operation
is involved here; I use it because it is the only documented seam that yields a
verbatim stderr payload with no `Error: ` prefix and an application-chosen
status, which SPEC.md's error table and 1-vs-2 exit codes both require.
`src/handlers.rs::to_failure`.

(b) Every command returns `Output::Artifact(...).allow_stdout()` carrying
pre-rendered bytes, so the template/BBCode pass never touches command output.
The registered templates in `src/main.rs` (`{{ report.note }}`) exist only to
satisfy build-time convention-template resolution and to render the empty-set
note; no command's stdout goes through them. This is a deliberate opt-out of
the framework's rendering layer, taken because SPEC.md specifies bytes.

(c) The empty-set stderr line rides the artifact *report* channel. Consequence
worth knowing: `get pods -n empty --output json` puts the framework's
`{"report": ..., "receipt": ...}` envelope on stderr instead of the prose line.
stdout is still empty and the exit is still 0. SPEC.md constrains `-o`, not
this combination of `-o` default with `--output json`, so I left it.

(d) `serde_json`'s `preserve_order` feature is load-bearing for `-o json` field
order, not a convenience. Without it `json!` sorts keys alphabetically and the
output stops matching SPEC.md's samples.
